title: Model endpoint resilience policy and adaptive load-shedding guidelines
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define and standardize per-endpoint and per-model SLO/SLI definitions, error budget enforcement, multi-region failover rules, circuit-breaker thresholds, and an adaptive load-shedding policy that can be applied consistently across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Purpose: reduce unplanned outages and maintain predictable degradation behavior for customer-facing model endpoints under load or infrastructure degradation.
background: We currently have several ad-hoc SLIs and SLOs across endpoints and model families. Past incidents showed inconsistent failover behavior between regions, and several customers experienced sudden 503 spikes with no graceful degradation (no degraded model fallback, cached responses, or shed-to-queue patterns). This ticket consolidates previous work and produces an actionable, testable policy and rollout plan.
proposal: 1) SLO/SLI taxonomy: latency p95/p99, availability (200 vs 2xx produced tokens), correctness gating (model inference errors), and tail queueing (requests queued > X ms). 2) Error budgets: define per-endpoint monthly and quarterly budgets; link to automatic throttle/fallback actions when budget burn rate exceeds thresholds. 3) Circuit breakers: hierarchical breakers (node pool, region, account) with configurable thresholds and cooldowns. 4) Adaptive load-shedding: progressive policy that prefers (a) prefix/KV cache hits, (b) reduced max_tokens and sketchier responses, (c) model-size fallback (e.g., large->medium->small), (d) best-effort cached or synthetic response, (e) request rejection with transparent reason and Retry-After header. 5) Multi-region failover: active-active routing with health probes, automatic RPO/RTO targets per tier, and manual override paths for enterprise customers.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): implement SLI collectors and dashboards for a sample of 10 endpoints across two regions; run chaos tests (GCP/EC2 sim failures)
Phase 1 (canary): enable adaptive load-shedding and circuit breakers for non-critical endpoints (low revenue) with telemetry and Kill-switch; observe error budget burn for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (select customers): opt-in enterprise customers and Dedicated pools; gather feedback and adjust thresholds
Phase 3 (general): enable defaults for all hosted endpoints; provide admin console controls and per-route overrides
Rollback: global toggle to disable adaptive shedding and revert to error responses; runbook in runbooks/reliability/endpoint-failover.md
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLI collection implemented and visible in Console for selected endpoints (latency p95/p99, availability, error rate)
A2: Error budgets computed automatically and displayed per endpoint with burn-rate alerts configured
A3: Circuit breakers trigger and log when thresholds hit; automated cooldown works as defined
A4: Adaptive load-shedding reduces overall tail latency and reduces error rate under controlled load tests by >=30% compared to baseline
A5: Multi-region failover exercises demonstrate RTO <= configured target and no silent data loss in 95% of test cases
A6: Documentation and console controls published; at least two production incidents show improved customer impact handling after rollout
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboard: Endpoint Resilience Overview (per-route and per-model tabs)
SLI metrics: total_requests, successful_responses(2xx), model_errors, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, queued_time_ms
Alerts: error budget burn rate > 2x for 1h, circuit-breaker trigger, cross-region failover initiated
Audit logs: record all automated load-shedding and fallback decisions with request_id
testing_plan: Unit tests for breaker state transitions and cooldowns
Integration tests for model-size fallback sequence and token budget adjustments
Load tests: step up to 3x peak traffic with and without adaptive shedding; compare tail latency and 5xx rate
Chaos experiments: region outage, node pool degradation, and KV cache loss
Customer simulation: replay production traffic for 7 days to measure error budget impact
migration_steps: 1) Instrument SLIs in runtime and Console UI for selected endpoints
2) Deploy circuit-breaker library behind a feature flag
3) Progressive enablement of adaptive shedding in staging then canary
4) Add per-route configuration defaults and exportable policy templates
5) Run compliance sweep for Dedicated/Private deployments to ensure policy is configurable by on-prem operators
